headline: Seasonal loss narrows as capacity and pricing lift revenue
summary_short: Q1 revenue rose 17.5% y/y to $1,053.7M on higher ocean capacity and pricing, while the seasonally soft net loss narrowed to $54.4M from $105.5M as operating income swung positive and currency losses eased.
summary_long: Q1 revenue grew 17.5% y/y to $1,053.7M on higher revenue per passenger-cruise-day, an added ocean ship boosting Capacity PCDs, and favorable itinerary mix. Operating income swung to $12.1M from a $9.3M loss as revenue growth outpaced cost growth across commissions, direct costs and vessel operating expenses. Net loss narrowed to $54.4M from $105.5M, helped by the $21.4M operating-income swing and a $24.3M drop in currency loss from euro debt/cash offsets, partly offset by a $5.2M impairment charge. The company's own Adjusted EBITDA rose to $104.8M from $72.8M. Cash and equivalents stood at $4,046.7M. Viking issues no formal numeric guidance; it disclosed 2026-season bookings 92% sold for both River and Ocean as of May 3, 2026.
